executive_assessment.text: Named parish poverty and sister-island water dependence help distinguish vulnerability within Grenada; the underlying indicators are historical or undated.
The draft highlights shelter protection risks. NAWASA's October 2026 report provides named-site water investments, with operational work and outcome verification still outstanding.

geographic_notes.text: The undated draft reports a 2020 national poverty-or-poverty-risk figure of 54.8%, with the highest rates in St. Mark and St. Andrew; weak savings and housing security increase household vulnerability.
Source dated not stated reports: FAO reports Carriacou livestock losses of 20% and 40% in the 1984 and 1992 droughts, and a 17% decline in national banana production during the 2009 drought.

Source dated not stated reports: The Ministry reports mainland dry-season daily yield of 31,800 m³ against demand of 54,600 m³; 91% of households in Carriacou and Petite Martinique use cisterns as main storage.

NAWASA reported in October 2026 that two 100,000-imperial-gallon tanks had been constructed at Belair and Mt. Royal. The estimated three-to-six-day storage buffer still depended on remaining operational connections and commissioning.

Source dated 2026-10-11 reports: NAWASA says the Mt. Royal communal rainwater retrofit serves about 56 households and 169 residents; storage was also added at Princess Royal Hospital and two medical stations.

Source dated 2026-10-11 reports: NAWASA reports over 300 farmers benefited across the tri-island state; on Carriacou, 18 received drip or micro-sprinkler support and 22 gained over 60,000 gallons of harvesting storage; 19 shade houses remain in phased installation.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. The official IOM climate-mobility assessment returned HTTP 403 and the Government-led Beryl PDNA PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit; no claims use indexed summaries.
A publicly linked IFRC rapid assessment was marked Internal on its cover and excluded; the WFP BRISP report PDF presented a bot-verification page.
No accessible country-specific source connected armed conflict or insecurity with climate impacts or adaptation delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The Government climate policy file is a December draft; its risk statements and proposed actions are not treated as adopted or measured outcomes.
These sources do not establish a countrywide causal estimate of climate-related conflict or violence.
The draft's policy period is internally inconsistent (2025–2030 versus 2025–2035); adoption and numerical source dates need human confirmation.
Shelter GBV is a stated protection risk, not observed incidence or evidence of armed conflict. Administrative procurement and coordination barriers are not attributed to insecurity.
